paris-le-de-france-escapes-vall-e-de-l-e.speedBand: 50–80 km/h riding core, local limits always win

sections.advice: Food stop near Saint-Arnoult-en-Yvelines → Scenic stretch near Nandy is the logistics leg. Watch junctions, villages and speed changes, then let the roadbook do its job: move you out of the clutter without spending your best attention too early.

Scenic stretch near Nandy → High point near Tournan-en-Brie is the technical section. Hairpins, gradients and mixed traffic can stack up quickly; use low drama inputs, stay wide of centre lines and expect buses or riders appearing exactly where optimism says they will not.

sections.to: Near Pont-Sainte-Maxence, on the way back
sections.advice: This High point near Tournan-en-Brie → Near Pont-Sainte-Maxence, on the way back stretch is for rhythm and scenery. Keep your head up, let the view breathe, and resist turning every open bend into a target. Stop once properly rather than half-stopping everywhere.

sections.advice: Photo stop in Blaincourt-lès-Précy → Le Raincy can flow quickly, but only if you keep village limits and junction sightlines sacred. Fast connectors are where rides get untidy when fatigue creeps in.

sections.advice: Ha Giang → Quan Ba Heaven Gate climbs about 1500 m in 33 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Quan Ba Heaven Gate → Dong Van drops about 1500 m over 56 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.

scenicChapters.title: Ha Giang Loop
scenicChapters.narrative: The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 62 km. 1500 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall. A steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not.

scenicChapters.title: Quan Ba Heaven Gate → Dong Van
scenicChapters.narrative: This is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else. 105 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it.

scenicChapters.title: Ha Giang Loop
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 1500 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

ha-giang-loop-ha-giang-ma-pi-leng-pass.story: From Hà Giang it runs 180 km to Thị Trấn Đồng Văn; allow about 2 h 30 of riding. The stops in between: Quan Ba Heaven and Dong Van. The highest point is about 1,500 m. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.

places-eining-weinberg-wachtturm-und-hei.provenance: CURATED FROM THE ARCHIVE: waypoints taken from the catalogued places the recipe names — a corridor between them, not a routed line. Distances between stops are great-circle with a road factor, not a routed measurement - the pipeline replaces them when it routes this line.
places-eining-weinberg-wachtturm-und-hei.story: 78 km from Neustadt an der Donau to Neustadt an der Donau, about 1 h 21 of riding. It goes by way of Watchtowers WP 15/11 to 15/26 and fortlets, Watchtowers WP 15/1 to 15/7 and back through Watchtowers WP 15/11 to 15/26 and fortlets. The line favours views over speed.
